title: The passive in other tenses
tagline: What's being built, what will be sent, and what must be worn.
why: Once you're comfortable with the basic passive, B1 Preliminary expects you to recognise and use it with continuous tenses, the past perfect, the future and modal verbs — the language of rules, ongoing repairs and predictions. These forms appear often in the Reading cloze parts and in formal emails, where 'must be worn' or 'will be sent' sounds far more natural than the active alternative.

hook.text: Someone broke the classroom window! Liam: "It's being fixed right now — look, a man's outside." Sofia: "It must be paid for by whoever did it." Nadia: "By tomorrow it will be replaced, Miss Vega said."
hook.ask: Find three passive verbs with an extra helper word before the past participle (being, must, will). What tense or meaning does each one add?

diagrams.title: Extra helpers in the passive
diagrams.caption: Whatever comes before be(ing) — will, must, is — the past participle always stays at the end.

rows.label: Meaning
cells: a fact or a finished action
an action in progress, happening now or then

rows.label: Present example
cells: The window is being fixed right now.

rows.label: Past example
cells: The car was being repaired when I arrived.

diagrams.title: How to add will, must or had

steps.label: Finish with the past participle
steps.ex: will be replaced / must be paid / had been broken

formula.chip: will be / must be / can be

head: Tense/meaning
Form
Example
rows: The window was being fixed when I saw it.
The window had been broken before we arrived.
The window will be replaced tomorrow.
It must be paid for by someone.
We had the window fixed by a professional.

use.point: Continuous passive: an action in progress

examples.text: The window is being fixed right now.
Our classroom was being painted when the fire alarm went off.
examples.note: an action in progress in the past

examples.text: The new library is being built next to the sports hall.

use.point: Past perfect passive: the earlier of two past events

examples.text: The window had been broken before the caretaker arrived.
examples.note: this happened before the other past event

examples.text: The report had already been sent when Miss Vega asked for it.
examples.note: already finished, earlier in the story

examples.text: Nobody knew the vase had been damaged until the next day.
examples.note: the damage happened earlier, discovered later

examples.text: The window will be replaced by Friday.
The new rules will be explained in tomorrow's assembly.
examples.note: future passive with a clear time

examples.text: All the broken glass will be removed this afternoon.

use.point: Modal passive: rules, permission and ability

examples.text: It must be paid for by whoever broke it.
Safety glasses should be worn near broken glass.
The old window can be seen in the school photos.
This kind of glass can't be repaired, only replaced.

watch_out.wrong: The window is fixing right now.
watch_out.right: The window is being fixed right now.
watch_out.why: An action in progress in the passive needs being + participle, not the active -ing form.
will needs be before the participle in the passive.

watch_out.wrong: It must paid for by someone.
watch_out.right: It must be paid for by someone.
watch_out.why: Every modal passive needs be between the modal and the participle.

watch_out.wrong: The window was broke before we arrived.
watch_out.right: The window had been broken before we arrived.
watch_out.why: The earlier of two past events needs the past perfect passive: had been + participle.

watch_out.wrong: The car was being repair when I arrived.
watch_out.right: The car was being repaired when I arrived.
watch_out.why: After being, use the past participle (repaired), not the base verb.

l1.why: The Spanish reflexive se + gerund becomes is/are being + past participle in English, not an active -ing verb.
Modal + be + participle — don't forget be, and don't add an extra pronoun after for.

l1.es: Ya se había roto antes de que llegáramos.
l1.wrong: It was broken before we arrived.
l1.right: It had been broken before we arrived.
l1.why: The earlier of two past actions needs the passive of the past perfect: had been + participle.
Future passive always needs be after will — will replaced is missing a word.

remember.trick: Add BE before every passive participle!
remember.tip: Will, must, can, had — none of them can touch the participle directly. Be always stands in between.

dialogue.title: The broken window

can_do: I can talk about actions in progress with the continuous passive (is/was being + participle).
I can use the passive with will, must, can and should to talk about the future, rules and possibility.
I can use the past perfect passive to show which of two past events happened first.
summary: Continuous passive = be + being + participle — an action in progress, now or in the past.
Past perfect passive = had been + participle — the earlier of two past events.
Modal passive = modal + be + participle (must be paid, can be seen, should be worn).
Whatever helper words come first, the past participle always stays at the very end. Note have + object + past participle (had the window fixed) — someone else did it for you.
